subject.title: fix(update): prevent compatible plugins from being skipped after npm-global upgrades

question: Should maintainers require complete npm-global update/restart proof and keep the linked issue open for its distinct runtime unknown-host variant before merging this bounded updater fix?
rationale: Source, focused tests, sibling behavior, and history support the implementation, but repository policy makes real behavior proof a merge gate for an external compatibility-sensitive update PR, and the linked issue now contains meaningful remaining behavior outside this patch.

options.title: Require proof and bound scope
options.body: Require a redacted lifecycle transcript and replace the closing relationship so the runtime unknown-host variant remains open.

options.title: Accept boundary proof
options.body: Explicitly accept the focused tests and compatibility-boundary output while still preserving separate tracking for the runtime unknown-host variant.

recommendation.title: Require proof and bound scope
recommendation.body: Require a redacted lifecycle transcript and replace the closing relationship so the runtime unknown-host variant remains open.

likelyOwner.reason: The predecessor co-authorship and broad historical ownership of the update and finalizer lifecycle make this the strongest available proof and scope decision route.
